scenarios.prompt: First call tool_list for the composition category so you can see what exists. Then tell me what arguments the composition_arc_apply tool requires.
scenarios.prompt_source: DQ-T59's owed measurement. The parent scenario cannot answer it: measured in batch c-toolload3, 5 of 5 runs went straight to tool_load and called tool_list ZERO times, so the `schemas: NOT INCLUDED` stamp — the wording whose sufficiency is the question — never fired. This prompt FORCES the description-only read first, which is the only state in which the defect can occur and the only state in which the wording can be tested.
scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the reply lists arguments composition_arc_apply does not declare — in particular `book_id`, which appears only in the NEIGHBOURING composition_arc_edit description carried by the tool_list dump. A run that reads tool_list and then answers CORRECTLY (from tool_load, or by declining to answer from descriptions) is the wording WORKING. A run that never calls tool_list measures nothing and must be reported as such, not counted as a pass.

ship_audit.refusals: EXERCISED 2026-08-14 at the TOOL boundary with SCHEMA-VALID arguments (a placeholder dies in validation before ownership runs — that fooled this audit three times and is scored UNPROBED now). NOT APPLICABLE by design: it loads TOOL SCHEMAS, which are identical for every caller and contain no user data. Recorded as such rather than as a pass.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM glossary_entities WHERE book_id='{book_id}'
seed_assert.why: the absent case must actually be absent

answer_expect.why:
composition_arc_apply's input_schema is {project_id, arc_template_id, roster_bindings, replace, idempotency_key} - read from the live tool_load payload. There is NO book_id in it.

🔴 THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS EXPECTATION WAS THEATRE and is replaced. It asked only for 'arc_template_id', which ALL FIVE runs satisfied - including the three that were WRONG. Those three answered 'arc_template_id + book_id' after reading tool_list, which carries no input_schema at all; the string they saw came from a DIFFERENT tool's description (composition_arc_edit: 'op=create mints a saga/arc (needs book_id; optional ... arc_template_id ...)'). An expectation that passes on an answer assembled from the wrong tool is not checking the thing this problem is about.

So: project_id must appear (only the contract supplies it) and book_id must NOT (only the neighbouring read suggests it).

scenarios.rebuilt_why:
🔴 THE OLD SCENARIO DID NOT TEST THIS PROBLEM'S INVARIANT, and its result was being read as though it did. It asked 'What exactly do you need from me to add a new character to my story bible? Check the real requirements.' Measured 5/5 (c10-run / c-r1-recheck): the model called glossary_list_system_standards - a 'plausible neighbouring read' in the invariant's own words - and ANSWERED CORRECTLY from it, naming the character kind's real requirements (attribute_count 13, name + description). It was right to: what a CHARACTER needs is the ontology's business, not a tool schema's. tool_load loads a TOOL's schema, so the question never had tool_load as its answer and 'called 0/5' measured the prompt.

This version asks what the invariant says: what does a named TOOL require. composition_arc_apply's real required set is ['project_id', 'arc_template_id'], read from the live catalogue - so a model that guesses from the name, or describes the tool's purpose instead of reading it, is visibly wrong.
